column1: # PG3D FPS Unlock graphics options: key, tab, label, hint, choices (value:label|...), Original, Balanced, Performance.
# Read by the launcher script and the app. Keys must match src/options.c; every graphics value is a ceiling on the game's own.
# Engine rows (tab engine) are not ceilings and not part of the presets: their preset columns are "-".

column4: The whole screen-effect stack on the game camera, plus the depth and HDR passes it needs. Off overrides the effects below.
Soft contact shadows in corners and creases. One of the costlier effects.
Glow around bright lights and muzzle flashes.
The map's color and tone curve. Off looks flatter.
Brightness adapting as you move between light and dark areas.
Chromatic aberration, vignette, film grain and lens distortion.
Background blur and blur while turning.
An extra pass over the scene that soft particles read. Effects that need it keep it while they are on.
Haze toward the horizon. Costs almost nothing; off changes the look.
Shadows cast by players, props and weapons.
Shadow distance, cascades and resolution. Medium: 25 m, 2 cascades. Low: 15 m, 1 cascade.
Lights drawn per pixel; the rest fall back to cheaper vertex lighting.
Reflection probes that re-render the scene, and screen-space reflections.
Smooths jagged edges by rendering extra samples.
Sharper textures at glancing angles.
How far models keep their detailed versions (LOD bias). The game uses 100, so it never simplifies.
Lower resolutions free video memory. Changing it can hitch once.
Bones per vertex on animated characters and weapons.
Smoke and sparks that fade into walls; needs the depth pass.
Extra pass for alpha-blended grass and leaves.
Raycast budget for particles that bounce off the world.
Unity runs its job workers below normal priority, so other apps can delay the jobs each frame waits for. High lifts them and the render thread.
Schedules the game’s GPU work ahead of other apps, such as browser video or a Discord stream.
